hypothesis: Designs evolved for locomotion on simulated land with evolvable (finely tuned) actuation phases spend a large fraction of their evaluation airborne, whereas designs evolved with first-order hydrodynamics (reduced gravity plus surface drag) and random clade-fixed phase offsets stay in contact with the ground almost all the time, as living deciliated organisms do (93.3% vs 52.7% ground contact in the paper).
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Tier A (published outputs or original simulator): mean ground-contact fraction of second-pass designs within 5 percentage points of 93.3% and of first-pass designs within 5 points of 52.7%, and second minus first >= 20 points. Tier B (simplified re-implementation, numbers not expected to match): mean contact fraction of second-pass champions >= 85% and second minus first >= 20 percentage points, with a permutation test p < 0.05 over trials. Contact at a time step = lowest node within 0.05 voxel lengths of the ground plane; fraction taken over the evaluation period.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered: refutes if second-pass contact fraction <= first-pass + 5 points (no improvement), or (Tier A) if either published mean differs from the paper's figure by > 15 points. Other outcomes are 'mixed'. If neither published outputs nor a runnable simulator is available, verdict inconclusive (data-unavailable).
planned_method: Tier A (preferred): the authors' public repository (Data Availability ref. 36; CC0) at the pinned commit; if it contains first- and second-pass evolved designs or logged contact data, compute contact fractions from those, re-simulating with the shipped CPU Voxelyze if it compiles. Tier B (fallback): the same pre-registered numpy mass-spring voxel re-implementation as levin-2020-xenobots-06 (5x5x4 workspace, population 32, 50 generations, 10 trials per pass). Pass 1 = land (full gravity, no drag) with per-voxel phase offsets in the genotype and mutated (Gaussian, SD 0.4*pi, clipped to [-pi/2, pi/2]). Pass 2 = water (gravity x 0.1, linear drag on exposed faces) with random phase offsets fixed per clade. Fitness = net horizontal displacement over 10 s at 2 Hz. Ground-contact fraction of each trial's final champion is the statistic; the two passes are compared by mean difference and a two-sided permutation test (10,000 permutations).

test_contract.expected_observation: Second-pass (water + random phase) champions are in ground contact for most of the evaluation (paper: 93.3%), first-pass (land + tuned phase) champions much less (paper: 52.7%).
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Second-pass champions are airborne as often as or more often than first-pass champions, or the published per-design numbers do not reproduce the reported means.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: The paper's deposited designs/outputs and simulator, or a re-implementation keeping the two stated changes (reduced gravity with surface drag; random clade-fixed phases versus evolvable phases) and the stated fitness. Scope is the simulation; the comparison with living organisms rests on the paper's observation that deciliated organisms always keep ventral contact.
test_contract.inference_method: Mean ground-contact fraction per pass over trials' champions; difference and permutation p-value; thresholds as in pass/fail criteria.
